description.p: A lightweight native GNOME application for Samsung Galaxy phones and tablets running a mainline Linux kernel. It configures the S Pen, the special keys of Samsung's keyboard covers, vibration feedback, fingerprints, dual boot and port updates.
Each page appears only when the device has the hardware behind it. Devices are described by small profiles; one without a profile still gets everything that can be detected on its own.

ul.li: First stable Galaxy Companion, with settings adapted to each Galaxy device.
New Android Dualboot app with corrected startup and Ubuntu 26 selection.
S Pen battery in GNOME and keyboard vibration at login and on the lock screen.
GNOME 50 support and keyboard-cover and Bluetooth fixes.

description.p: Pre-release of Galaxy Companion as its own project; 1.0.0 will be the first official release. Tab Companion from the Galaxy Tab S9 Ultra port becomes Galaxy Companion: device profiles select the pages and hardware for each Samsung device, so the same application runs on the Galaxy Tab S9 Ultra, the Galaxy S9+ and devices without a profile, and settings carry over from Tab Companion.

A home page shows the device, its processor and memory; the app updates itself from its own releases. Status LED rules per app, battery, charging and media with quiet hours; a battery charge limit where it is confirmed to work; the Bixby button mapped like the S Pen button; dual boot on any device whose profile lists its boot partitions, with the Dualboot Android app saving Android's side.

System updates can install an Ubuntu release upgrade: a build ZIP whose manifest declares one hands off to the migration backend it carries, from the port's published release or from a local file after its complete SHA-256 is shown and confirmed. A failed offline update configures the packages it had unpacked before restoring the previous boot images, and the frozen offline runner carries every module it needs.
